source.title: Post-Hoc Concept Disentanglement: From Correlated to Isolated Concept Representations
source.authors: Eren Erogullari; S. Lapuschkin; W. Samek; Frederik Pahde

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies entanglement between concept activation vector (CAV) directions, not polysemanticity of individual neurons or any of the listed versions. Its results concern a related representation-level construct.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CAV cosine similarities and orthogonalization results in image models. These do not measure whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs, so they are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study measures cosine similarity and orthogonality between supervised concept activation vectors (CAV directions), not whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. It neither tests nor relies on neuron polysemanticity. It only mentions superposition in passing, citing Toy Models of Superposition. Its findings concern a related but different construct: entanglement of linear concept directions driven by dataset co-occurrence.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors add that orthogonalized CAVs allow concepts to be added or removed in isolation without affecting correlated concepts in steering tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains and fine-tunes supervised CAV directions with an added non-orthogonality penalty. It does not use the original studies' neuron-level analyses or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The orthogonality-versus-AUROC trade-off depends on the loss weight α; larger α improves orthogonality but can sharply reduce AUROC. The authors also report different per-concept AUROC changes during optimization.

fits_no_version.finding: In VGG16 and ResNet18, CAVs for frequently co-occurring concepts (e.g. smiling, high cheekbones) are highly similar. A non-orthogonality loss makes them near-orthogonal with a slight AUROC drop, depending on α.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In image classifiers, supervised concept directions for correlated concepts are entangled, and post-hoc orthogonalization can reduce this entanglement while largely preserving concept separability.

record.problems: The study's measures are CAV direction cosine similarity, orthogonality, and AUROC, not neuron-level polysemanticity. Key metric values are presented in figures without numerical values in the text; uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports per-concept AUROC changes, qualitative CAV heatmaps, concept insertion with a Diffusion Autoencoder, and P-ClArC shortcut-suppression results in Sections 4.2–5.2 and Figures 4–9. These findings concern individual CAV behavior or application outputs rather than neuron polysemanticity; no additional rows are included.

untested.parts: Individual neurons in image classifiers responding to unrelated inputs; the study analyses CAV directions only.
All parts; no language-model MLP neurons are studied.
Superposition as the cause of neuron polysemanticity; the study attributes CAV entanglement to dataset co-occurrence, not neuron capacity.
All parts; there is no comparison of neuron polysemanticity across activations or architectures.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given, because no row measures neuron-level polysemanticity. Rows r2–r9 report the study's own method's performance; their states were reset to cannot_determine because they have no claim version to bear on.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarities among CAV directions trained separately.
rows.measure: Pairwise CAV cosine similarity / concept-direction entanglement
rows.value: The text reports highly similar CAVs for concepts that frequently co-occur; the similarity matrix is shown in Figure 2.
rows.note: This measures concept directions, not individual neurons. The paper gives examples of co-occurring concepts whose CAVs align.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned CAVs for 300 epochs with the orthogonality loss.
rows.note: The authors describe a drastic increase and near-perfect or complete orthogonalization across the experiments; numerical values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's performance, not a measurement of a version's effect. The value is figure-only; 'observed' only means the orthogonality goal was met.
